description: Femme au chapeau pastel over traces of pencil 38.5 x 32cm (15 3/16 x 12 5/8in).
provenance: Private collection, UK. | Private collection, London (acquired from the above circa 2015). |  | Edmond Aman-Jean enrolled at the École des Beaux-Arts in 1880, where he studied with Henri Lehmann, and later trained under Pierre Puvis de Chavannes, assisting him on The Sacred Grove in Lyon. He shared a studio with Georges Seurat during the late 1870s who draw a portrait of him, now in the collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art. In 1886, he was awarded a scholarship to study in Rome, after which he became associated with Symbolist literary circles, including Stéphane Mallarmé, Paul Verlaine, and Villiers de l'Isle Adam. Aman-Jean established himself primarily through portraits of women, while also producing murals for public buildings such as the Sorbonne, as well as lithographs and posters. |  | He was a regular exhibitor at the Société Nationale des Beaux-Arts, eventually serving on its jury, and participated in the Salons de la Rose+Croix during the early 1890s, for which he designed posters. A portrait of his wife exhibited in 1893, depicting her with her hair styled low at the sides of her face, attracted wide public attention and was credited with sparking a fashion trend in Paris. He also collaborated internationally, joining Whistler's International Society of Sculptors, Painters and Gravers exhibition in London in 1898. |  | In the later years of his career, Aman-Jean co-founded the Salon des Tuileries in 1923, consolidating his position within the Parisian art world. He also held a significant role as a teacher, instructing artists such as Charles Sydney Hopkinson, Theodor Pallady, and Nicolae Tonitza. His work demonstrates a wide range of artistic influences, from Japanese art to English Pre-Raphaelites. Through his life, his friendships and collaborations connected him to leading figures of the period including Seurat, Ernest Laurent, and Paul Verlaine.

title: Portrait of Philip Harvey
description: Portrait of Philip Harvey signed with initials and dated 'H.S.T./Nov 1883' (upper left) oil on panel 33 x 23.5cm (13 x 9 1/4in).
provenance: The artist's studio. | Private collection, UK (gifted by the artist and thence by descent). | Anon. sale, David Lay Auctions, Penzance, 25 August 2023, lot 325. |  | Henry Scott Tuke settled in the fishing town of Newlyn in 1883, taking up residence on Trewarveneth Street. His studio, owned by local fisherman and sailmaker Philip Harvey, was a modest but practical space. Still serving as a sail loft for Harvey's equipment, it also provided Tuke with a place to work. The setting proved ideal for his practice, as the rhythms of daily life in the town deeply influenced his art, much like it did for other members of the Newlyn School.

title: Portrait of a girl seated, in a fur trimmed coat with a bow in her hair
description: Portrait of a girl seated, in a fur trimmed coat with a bow in her hair signed, inscribed and dated 'S. Rodriguez/Paris. Marzo 1884' oil on canvas 150 x 113cm (59 1/16 x 44 1/2in).
provenance: Private collection, UK.  |  | Little information is available on the life and relatively brief artistic career of Argentinian born Severo Rodriguez Etchart.  He received formal artistic training firstly in Buenos Aires before travelling to Turin where he studied at the Albertina Academy. His artistic talent then took him to Paris where he studied at the Académie Julian under Tony Robert-Fleury and the celebrated French master William-Adolphe Bouguereau. He was an exhibitor at the Paris Salon, and collection of his work can be found in the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes in Buenos Aires.  The present lot depicts a young girl seated in a relaxed, thoughtful pose. She is elegantly dressed, her outfit complimented with touches of gold in the form of a small gold chain and jewellery. The rich yet subtle reds, browns and blues of her clothing give the impression of warmth and comfort, yet also not inconsiderable wealth. While the background is deliberately unstated, closer inspection of the gold wall reveals a more intricate pattern, and hints of a rich gold interior are left by the artist. It has been suggested that the sitter for this portrait may be the artist's daughter.

title: Summer
description: Summer signed in Cyrillic (lower right); further signed, titled and dated '2018' (verso) oil on canvas 110 x 100cm (43 5/16 x 39 3/8in).
provenance: Private collection, UK. |  | Born in 1962 in Zagorsk into the family of the renowned Russian artist Leonid Demin, Andrey Demin was immersed in art from an early age. At just ten years old, he was sent to art school, where he worked primarily on still-life paintings alongside more experienced artists. This formative experience deeply influenced his artistic development. |  | As Andrey himself recalls: | "I saw my first paintings even before I could walk. I communicated with professional painters even before I learnt to talk. What else could I have become, if not an artist?" |  | Widely exhibited today, Andrey's work first gained public attention in the late 1990s at Roy Miles and later at Paul Hawkins Gallery on Davies Street, Mayfair, London. His extensive travels across Britain, Germany, Switzerland, and Cyprus have profoundly influenced his landscape paintings. He draws particular inspiration from the natural beauty and mythology of the countries he visits. |  | Trained in the traditional Russian Impressionist style, Andrey's canvases are bathed in light, with the misty colors of countryside and seascapes lending a delicate atmosphere to his work. His serene landscapes evoke a wistful innocence, inviting the viewer into a contemplative, almost dreamlike world. |  | What sets Andrey's paintings apart is their straightforwardness, technical excellence, and accessibility, qualities that have contributed to his broad international appeal and success.
